business-owner-tax-planning/index.html.heading: Tax advisory for owners with several decisions to coordinate
business-owner-tax-planning/index.html.body:
When you own several businesses, a tax decision in one entity can affect owner pay, retirement funding, property cash flow and your household return. Start with an ownership and income map, then agree on which alternatives need modeling and who will carry out each action.

When a coordinated engagement fits

  • Several entities or K-1s with different owners, states or preparers.
  • Business profits alongside rental properties or a building used by the business.
  • An acquisition, ownership change or sale that needs review before documents are signed.
  • A need for a second opinion on an existing plan and its implementation.

Define the work before starting

Ask your proposal to identify the records and entities reviewed, written recommendations and assumptions, alternatives to compare, action deadlines, and the person responsible for each filing or professional handoff. Decide how AE will coordinate with your existing CPA, bookkeeper and other specialists.

Strategic Tax Advisory: $7,800. Complex Tax Advisory: $9,800. Returns, amendments, cost segregation and additional work are separately scoped. Confirm deliverables, implementation responsibilities and the support period in your written agreement. Review fees and engagement scope.

Explore your next decision

  • Planning for multiple businesses and owner-level income
  • A second opinion on your current tax strategy
  • Business income and rental property planning

physician-tax-planning/index.html.heading: Practice income, property and retirement in one planning discussion
physician-tax-planning/index.html.body:
A profitable practice can involve several competing uses for cash: staffing, owner compensation, retirement funding, an acquisition and a building purchase. Bring these decisions into one forecast before committing to a plan.

Questions for your advisory scope

  • Which practice entities, owner returns and states need coordinated review?
  • What changes if you buy a practice and its building together?
  • Who models retirement funding alongside operating reserves and debt payments?
  • Who coordinates the recommendations with your preparer and plan administrator?

Discuss an engagement that identifies written alternatives, assumptions, decision dates and implementation owners.

real-estate-tax-strategy-business-owners.title: Tax Advisor for Business Owners With Rental Properties | AE Tax Advisors
real-estate-tax-strategy-business-owners.description: Coordinate business income, rental portfolios and property purchases. Review usable deductions, implementation responsibilities and advisory fees.
real-estate-tax-strategy-business-owners.heading: One advisory scope for your business and rental portfolio
real-estate-tax-strategy-business-owners.body:
If you own an operating business and rental properties, start with the full income picture. A study, entity election or purchase should be evaluated against the owner-level return, cash commitments and future plans.

Make the coordination explicit

  • Map business ownership, property entities, states and current preparers.
  • Reconcile income, existing depreciation and suspended losses before evaluating more study work.
  • Compare purchase, refinance, hold and sale scenarios using documented assumptions.
  • Assign the advisory review, property study, bookkeeping and each return to a named professional.

The written proposal should identify the properties and entities covered, alternatives to model, required records and implementation deadlines.
